key_insight: Fuse-PINN combines finite-element methods and neural networks to enable scalable multi-GPU simulations of nonlinear PDEs.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to parallel physics-informed simulation of complex nonlinear systems, demonstrated on models relevant to magnetic confinement fusion rather than solid mechanics.
method: Formulates a mathematically grounded Finite-Element-Method for Neural Networks (FEM-NN).
Implements modular GPU-based parallelisation in Fuse-PINN.
Uses Energy Natural Gradient Descent for high-precision convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-perfect scaling on multi-GPU runs as problem size increases, with demonstrations including nonlinear convective models exhibiting fine-scale dynamics.
watch_item: Scaling is reported for increasing problem sizes; fixed-size scaling, hardware requirements, and performance against conventional FEM solvers are not specified in the abstract.
paper_title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs
